chapters.title: Lists in Templates
chapters.subtitle: Liquid filters for containers and their items

steps.text: A list is a content item that holds other content items, such as a blog and its posts. This video shows how templates read a list: the ListPart template, and the three Liquid filters container, list_items, and list_count.
A list is a content item with a ListPart. Each item inside the list carries a ContainedPart, which stores the id of its list, the content type of that list, and the position of the item in it.
The Lists module adds three Liquid filters that read this relationship: container, list_items, and list_count. They work in any Liquid template, not only in the templates of a list.

chapters.title: The ListPart template
chapters.subtitle: Rendering the items of a list

steps.text: To display a list, the ListPart shape receives a ListPartViewModel. Its ContentItems property holds one page of published items, and its Pager property holds the links to the other pages.

The Blog Theme overrides the template of this shape in Blog-ListPart.liquid. It loops over Model.ContentItems, builds the Summary display of each item, and renders Model.Pager. Because of its name, it applies to the Blog content type only.

chapters.title: The container filter
chapters.subtitle: From an item to its list

steps.text: The container filter takes a content item and returns the list that holds it. In the Blog recipe, the Autoroute pattern of a blog post uses it to start each post's address with the name of its blog.
If an item is not in a list, or its list is not published, container returns the item itself. The input must be a content item: anything else raises an exception.
The list_items filter returns the content items of a list, and list_count counts them. Give either one a content item, or the content item id of the list as a string.

Only published items count, so an item that exists only as a draft is left out. The filters do not page: list_count counts the whole list, and list_items returns all of it, sorted by the order stored in each ContainedPart.

chapters.title: A template that uses them
chapters.subtitle: All three on a blog post page

steps.text: Let's use all three in the template for blog posts. The assign tag saves the blog that container returns for the current post, and the template prints its title as a link, followed by its number of published posts from list_count.
Then list_items returns the published posts of that blog, assign saves them in a variable, and a for loop prints a link to each one, with display_url for the address and display_text for the title.

Add this block at the end of the post template: Content-BlogPost.liquid in a theme, or a template named Content__BlogPost under Design, Templates. A template saved in the admin takes priority over the theme file of the same name, so it must be complete.
In the admin, Design, Templates lists the template under its name, Content__BlogPost. It applies to the page of every blog post.
On the page of a blog post, the block follows the content. The heading links back to the blog, and list_count reports three published posts, although the blog also holds a draft.
Below the count, the loop prints a link to each published post. The draft is missing from the list, because list_items returns published items only.

chapters.title: In Razor
chapters.subtitle: The same queries in a view

steps.text: In a Razor view, the Orchard helper offers the same two queries: QueryListItemsAsync and QueryListItemsCountAsync. Both take the id of the list.
An optional second argument is a predicate on the content item index. It replaces the default of published items: a predicate on the Latest property of the index includes drafts.

That is how templates read a list: the ListPart shape renders one page of items, container finds the list of an item, and list_items and list_count work on every published item of a list. Thanks for watching.
